newsitem.title: USA: Tone of U.S. budget talks "positive" -White House.
newsitem.headline: Tone of U.S. budget talks "positive" -White House.

text.p: White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters on Thursday that budget talks continue between White House and congressional negotiators, describing their tone as "constructive."

"The tone of the meetings has been very constructive and positive," McCurry said, saying the talks cover both tax and spending legislation. "They will likely continue throughout the balance of the day and most likely in the days ahead."

"One of the things we're doing now is to assess what likelihood there is that we could make progress before the congressional summer recess, and I don't believe that's clear at this point," McCurry added.

Negotiators for the White House and Congress are seeking to hammer out tax and spending legislation that would enact the balanced-budget agreement reached between President Bill Clinton and the Republican-controlled Congress in May.
Congress is scheduled to begin its regular summer recess during the first week of August.
